description: A Southern farmhouse front entry photographed at standing eye-level with a normal lens in a three-quarter corner composition. The facade features painted white brick with a rough coursed texture, dark-stained exposed wood ceiling beams running along the porch soffit, and a dramatic arched doorway with a rounded brick arch surround framing a pair of divided-light solid walnut double doors with oil-rubbed bronze hardware. A black-shuttered double-hung window sits to the right of the entry door. A warm amber glow emanates from the antique brass wall lantern position between the door and the window, the frosted glass casting a honeyed light onto the white brick and the porch floor. The landing is laid in worn terracotta or old red brick pavers. A simple natural oak rocking chair with a white linen pillow occupies the porch beside the door. White hydrangea blooms in full flower spill from wicker baskets and galvanized metal planters arranged lavishly around the base of the steps and flanking both sides of the entry, creating an abundant, cottage-garden welcome. Lush green foliage fills the background between the house and mature trees. The palette is classic and restrained — white brick, warm walnut brown, antique brass, and pure white bloom — with deep green garden foliage. The atmosphere is welcoming, traditionally Southern American, and gently festive.
